title: Quimbo: 3-in-1 coffee may be taxed if sugar content remains high
summary: House Committee on Ways and Means Chairperson Miro Quimbo on Friday warned that 3-in-1 coffee could be subjected to taxation in three years if manufacturers fail to reduce the sugar content of their…

blocks.text: House Committee on Ways and Means Chairperson Miro Quimbo on Friday warned that 3-in-1 coffee could be subjected to taxation in three years if manufacturers fail to reduce the sugar content of their products.
Unlike regular coffee, 3-in-1 coffee contains sugar and other caloric ingredients, making it a potential candidate for inclusion in the sweetened beverage tax, he explained in an online interview.
Quimbo said 3-in-1 coffee was exempted from the sweetened beverage tax when it was first implemented several years ago because it was widely consumed by ordinary Filipinos.
However, he noted that manufacturers have since increased the sugar content of their products.
Some members of the House of Representatives have proposed imposing a tax on 3-in-1 coffee, Quimbo said.
However, he said his committee was not inclined to support the proposal, citing the product's widespread consumption among lower-income Filipinos.
Still, Quimbo stressed the need to consider the health effects of excessive sugar consumption.

"Hindi kami puwedeng walang gawin pagdating diyan dahil kailangan natin kumbinsihin ang mga manufacturers na babaan o bawasan nila yung tamis nito. Kasi nagiging cause din ito ng diabetes na siyang nagiging pangunahing cause ng death na noncommunicable diseases sa ating bansa," Quimbo said.

(We cannot simply do nothing about this because we need to convince manufacturers to reduce the sweetness or sugar content of their products. This can also contribute to diabetes, which is one of the leading causes of death from noncommunicable diseases in our country.)
He said manufacturers could be given a three-year transition period to reformulate their products and lower their sugar content.
Otherwise, 3-in-1 coffee products exceeding a measurable sugar threshold could be subjected to taxation after the transition period, he added.
"But today, we are not going to tax it," Quimbo said.

In a statement, Presidential Legislative Liaison Office Secretary Joey Salceda said proposals to extend the sweetened beverage tax to sweetened coffee, including 3-in-1 mixes, should be evaluated on their own merits and not based on declining alcohol tax revenues.
"Sin taxes are punitive by design. They are meant to discourage socially undesirable behavior, not to compensate for declining revenues from other sin taxes," he said. —VBL, GMA News
